The respondent Nos.1-3 having replied to the same on 5-2-2007 expressing reservation as to the genuineness of the legal notice and its contents (Annexure-'D-1'), the petitioners were consequentially constrained to file this application. At the time of filing of this application it was also brought to the notice of the Court that the Company has recently come into possession of certain land that was denied for a long time. The history of the use of such land situated in District-Chittagong, Mouza-Joypahar RS-96, Khatian No. 379 and 380, BS Khatian No. 65, Dag No.616 and measuring 02.10 acres by the Respondent No. 1 Company, and as depicted in the Application, that the Company requested the then Burma Oil Company Limited, subsequently renamed Padma Oil Company Limited, to set up a petrol pump with attendant facilities as a permanent establishment on the said land. Thereafter, the Company entered into a lease agreement for an initial period of fifteen years commencing on 10-1-1969 with a provision for a renewal of the lease. It is stated that Padma Oil Company on 20-11-1972 executed a license agreement in favour of M/s Abu Taher & sons, a proprietary firm, of which one late Moulvi Abu Taher, and husband of late Saleha Khatun, was the proprietor. The petitioners proposed renewal of the lease to the Company in due course but no decision was given by the Company and a civil suit being Title Suit No.144 of 1998 was filed by M/s Abu Taher & Sons before the Court of Subordinate Judge, First Court Sadar, Chittagong praying for a permanent injunction and that Suit is still pending. Presently, the petitioners are operating the said petrol pump. It has been the petitioners' appeal that they be allowed to continue with the business activities of the petrol pump for the welfare of the Company itself and that the Respondent No. 3 who has allegedly been acting against the interests of the Company be restrained from hindering such activities. It is noted that it is upon a consideration of this application in its totality and of the prayers made to that effect that in admitting this Application on 15-2-2007 the Court issued an ad interim order so restraining the respondent Nos.1, 2 and 3. 

 8. It is also stated that subsequently, and pursuant to the office memo No. 20(Dha)262/ 2006-Beuma No. 26/04-3252/SA dated 20-11-2006 issued by the Office of the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong the possession of the Company's said properties as identified in RS Khatian No. 96 and RS Plot No. 379 and 380 measuring 2.10 acres of land along with the petrol pump in question thereon were duly handed over to the Company on 13-12-2006 by the concerned officials of the office of the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong by evicting the occupants there under including M/s Abu Taher and Sons. The Company have duly taken over the possession of the same on 13-12-2006 by erecting a boundary wall surrounding the petrol pump with the fact of the handing over of possession being informed to all concerned by the office of the Deputy Commissioner vide its memo bearing No. 224(9)(1)/Bichar dated 17-12-2006 (Annexure-'7'). It is against this backdrop the Respondent Nos. 1-3 have since been in possession of the said properties including the petrol pump in question. It is stated in this regard that the petitioners having accordingly being lawfully evicted from the petrol pump in question on 13-12-2006, and long before the filling of this Application on 14-2-2007, the ad-interim order of this Court dated 15-2-2007 was obtained by misleading the Court and upon suppression of material facts. It is on the basis of these facts and contentions that the respondents submit that the Company has no legal obligation to register the petitioners' names as shareholders and, as such this application is liable to be rejected.
